history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration, at the level of the Headquarters Committee on Contracts, issue an annual report based on its reviews, focusing on key areas of improvement and good practices that should be shared widely.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. Based on the Board’s findings and in the context of the advisory role of the Headquarters Committee on Contracts, the Administration took a risk-based approach and established procedures for ongoing feedback from the Committee to relevant United Nations offices. For example, the Chair of the Committee has monthly meetings with the Assistant Secretary-General for Supply Chain Management and the Director of the Procurement Division concerning areas that require attention. When warranted, the Chair of the Headquarters Committee on Contracts proposes revisions to the Procurement Manual to address any shortfalls observed and to share good practices among procurement practitioners in the United Nations Secretariat. In addition, heads of entities receive copies of minutes of meetings of the Headquarters Committee on Contracts for cases submitted, containing the Committee’s advice as well as any other recommendations that may have emerged from cases reviewed. The Chair of the Committee participates in the formulation of amendments to the Procurement Manual and in the procurement delegation of authority, and attends conferences of chief procurement officers and similar forums, to ensure that compliance aspects are duly taken into account and proactively shared. The Administration also wishes to advise, with reference to the Board’s specific finding that some procurement officers were seeking and obtaining an exemption to competitive bidding prior to conducting a solicitation while others first conducted a solicitation exercise and then requested an exemption through the process of vetting and approving the recommendation for an award, that such inconsistent practices have been addressed. In particular, the delegation of procurement authority matrix was updated in 2023 to streamline the process by allowing the justification for informal methods of solicitation under financial rule 105.16 (a) (x) to be combined with the statement of award when seeking approval of award, and the Procurement Manual was amended in 2024 to clarify that contract amendments governed by financial rule 105.13 are not to be construed as exceptions to formal methods of solicitation and therefore do not require a waiver of competitive bidding.
history.board_assessment: Although an annual report was not issued pursuant to the recommendation, the Board acknowledges that there has been a change in context and that actual progress has been evidenced through the documents provided by the Administration. Therefore, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
